name: --add-dir
description: Grant Claude read and edit access to one or more additional existing directories for the current session.

examples.explanation: Work across sibling application and library directories.

when_to_use: Use when a task spans directories outside the initial working tree.
when_not_to_use: Do not assume most .claude configuration is discovered from added directories.

conditions: Every supplied path must already exist as a directory.

name: --agent
description: Select a configured custom agent for the current session, overriding the agent setting.

examples.explanation: Start the session using the configured security-reviewer agent.

when_to_use: Use when a task should begin with one specific custom agent's tools and instructions.

conditions: The named agent must be available in the current configuration.

name: --agents
description: Define custom subagents for the invocation using JSON fields compatible with subagent frontmatter plus a prompt.

examples.command: claude --agents '{"reviewer":{"description":"Reviews code","prompt":"You are a code reviewer"}}'
examples.explanation: Define a reviewer subagent for this invocation without creating an agent file.

when_to_use: Use for temporary or automation-supplied subagent definitions.
when_not_to_use: Use agent files for definitions that should be maintained and reused.

conditions: Startup JSON validation requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

name: --allowed-tools
description: Specify tool permission rules that can execute without an approval prompt; this does not restrict the tools available to Claude.

examples.explanation: Allow common read-only repository inspection without prompts.

when_to_use: Use to reduce prompts for narrowly scoped, understood operations.
when_not_to_use: Use --tools to restrict tool availability; allowed-tools only changes permission prompting.

conditions: Managed policy can further restrict permissions.

name: --dangerously-skip-permissions
description: Start in bypassPermissions mode and skip Claude Code permission prompts.

examples.explanation: Run without Claude Code prompts inside a separately isolated disposable environment.

when_to_use: Use only where an external sandbox already contains the risks of unrestricted agent actions.
when_not_to_use: Do not use on a normal developer workstation when scoped permission rules are sufficient.

conditions: Equivalent to --permission-mode bypassPermissions and may be blocked by managed policy.

name: --disallowed-tools
description: Remove whole tools or deny scoped operations that match the supplied permission rules.

examples.explanation: Deny matching removal commands and remove the Edit tool from context.

when_to_use: Use to impose explicit session-level tool restrictions in addition to normal approvals.

name: --effort
description: Set the reasoning effort for the current session, subject to the selected model's available levels.

examples.explanation: Use high effort for a difficult architecture task.

when_to_use: Use to trade latency and usage for deeper reasoning on a demanding task.
when_not_to_use: Do not assume every listed effort level is supported by every model.

conditions: Available effort levels depend on the model; ultracode requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later.

name: --fork-session
description: Create a new session identifier instead of reusing the original when continuing or resuming a conversation.

examples.explanation: Branch the named session into a new resumable conversation.

when_to_use: Use to explore an alternative from an earlier conversation without changing the original session.

name: --json-schema
description: Validate the final non-interactive result against a supplied JSON Schema after the agent completes its workflow.

examples.explanation: Return a validated object containing a summary field.

when_to_use: Use when automation needs a predictable validated result after Claude finishes using tools.
when_not_to_use: Do not use for interactive sessions; this flag is for print mode.

name: --max-budget-usd
description: Stop a print-mode workflow when API spend, including subagent spend, reaches the specified dollar cap.

examples.command: claude -p --max-budget-usd 5.00 "analyze and fix the failing integration tests"
examples.explanation: Run a headless task with a five-dollar API-spend ceiling.

when_to_use: Use to bound cost for unattended API-backed workflows.
when_not_to_use: Do not treat the cap as a guarantee that a task will complete within the limit.

conditions: Print mode only; full subagent cap enforcement requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later.

name: --mcp-config
description: Load MCP server definitions for the invocation from JSON files or inline JSON strings.

examples.explanation: Load the project's MCP servers for this session.

when_to_use: Use to provide temporary or automation-specific MCP servers without changing persistent configuration.

conditions: Print-mode startup waiting for pending servers requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later.

name: --output-format
description: Select text, JSON, or streaming JSON output for print mode.

examples.explanation: Return a machine-readable JSON result for a headless prompt.

when_to_use: Use JSON formats when another program will consume Claude's output.
when_not_to_use: Do not expect output-format to structure the answer to a custom schema; use --json-schema for that.

name: --worktree
description: Create an isolated Git worktree under the repository's .claude/worktrees directory and start Claude there.

examples.explanation: Create and enter an isolated feature-auth worktree.

when_to_use: Use to isolate concurrent or experimental changes from the primary checkout.
when_not_to_use: Do not use outside a Git repository or when the task must modify the current checkout directly.

conditions: Requires Git; branching from a GitLab merge request requires Claude Code v2.1.233 or later.
